en.headline: Housewife loses nearly HK$1.3 million in hotel booking job scam
en.dek: Police said the woman made more than 30 transfers over five days after being lured by promises of commissions, with over 20 similar cases reported in the past week.
body: A housewife lost nearly HK$1.3 million after falling for an online job scam involving bogus hotel booking tasks, police said on Monday.

According to the force's CyberDefender account, the woman was contacted via WhatsApp after responding to a social media advertisement. Scammers sent a fake website link and instructed her to transfer money to top up an account to complete tasks. She initially withdrew about HK$10,000 in commission before further transfers were demanded, including a claimed unfreezing fee.

Police said more than 20 online employment scam cases were reported in the past week, with total losses exceeding HK$3.2 million. Officers urged the public to be wary of job offers promising high commissions for simple online tasks.

zh.headline: 家庭主婦誤信酒店刷單騙案 五日損失近130萬元
zh.dek: 警方指事主五日內轉賬逾30次，過去一周接獲逾20宗同類網上求職騙案，總損失逾320萬元。
body: 一名家庭主婦誤墮網上求職騙案，進行虛假酒店預訂刷單任務，五日內損失近130萬港元，警方周一表示。
根據警方守網者專頁，事主在社交平台回應招聘廣告後，騙徒透過WhatsApp聯絡，並發送虛假網站連結，指示她轉賬為帳號增值以完成任務。事主起初成功提取約1萬元佣金，其後再被要求轉賬，包括聲稱的解凍費。
警方指過去一周接獲逾20宗網上求職騙案，總損失逾320萬港元。警方呼籲市民提防承諾高佣金的簡單網上工作。
